findings.detail: The training path loads a single precomputed sentence_t5.npy embedding per item and selects rows for train targets. It never loads metadata text, creates stochastic/dropout views, encodes M views, quantizes their mean, or uses a validation split to select lambda. Thus the core proposed uncertainty-aware tokenizer is absent; this is effectively the baseline RQ-VAE path.
findings.reproduction: Run main with the configured inputs and inspect the batch loop at lines 299-304: each batch is one fixed embedding tensor and receives exactly one model forward. There is no call to uncertainty_agreement anywhere in train_rqvae.py or model code.
findings.correction: Construct multiple independent training-only metadata views per item, encode and quantize all views, optimize the stated RQ loss on the view mean plus lambda times the variance-weighted agreement term, and select lambda on validation data. Export by quantizing the mean view embedding.

findings.detail: The proposed agreement penalty is not trainable as implemented: variance is explicitly detached, and token disagreement is a Boolean inequality on integer code indices, so the returned value has no gradient path to encoder or quantizer parameters. Moreover, this function is never called by the trainer, and the trainer loss is only the baseline reconstruction plus quantization loss (train_rqvae.py:302-304). A finite scalar penalty alone cannot change codes or parameters.
findings.reproduction: With encoded_views=torch.randn(2,1,3,requires_grad=True) and token_views=torch.tensor([[[0]],[[1]]]), uncertainty_agreement(...) returns a scalar without requires_grad; calling .backward() raises because it has no grad_fn. A trainer backward therefore receives no gradient contribution from this term (indeed, no call to it).
findings.correction: Wire the agreement objective into the actual training loss and provide a differentiable surrogate/gradient mechanism for cross-view code consistency (while retaining hard-code agreement as a metric if desired). Verify finite loss and nonzero gradients reaching intended encoder/codebook parameters on a multi-view batch.
